strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear criteria for simulation-ready tabletop scenes; identifies genuine gap in existing methods for high-density, collision-free layouts
Exceptionally strong empirical results: near-zero collision rates (0.42% vs 8-17% for baselines), 83.13% user preference with 128 participants, consistent improvements across visual quality metrics
Novel two-stage pose and scale alignment approach (DRO + TSA) effectively decouples complex 3D reasoning; RMA-Score anchor selection is clever and well-motivated

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple evaluation dimensions, large user study with randomized controls, thorough ablations demonstrating necessity of components, comparison with relevant baselines
Pragmatic system design using existing models (ChatGPT, Seedream, Hunyuan3D) enables immediate deployment without retraining; training-free approach is practical
Excellent presentation and reproducibility efforts: detailed supplementary materials with stage-wise intermediate outputs, complete prompts, efficiency analysis, promised code release
Practical utility demonstrated through real-world image reconstruction, scene editing, and robotic manipulation task execution in physics simulation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily a system combining existing models (GroundedSAM-v2, Hunyuan3D, ChatGPT); DRO is standard differentiable rendering with tri-modal loss; TSA relies on MLLM predictions and handcrafted heuristics rather than principled geometric reasoning

Heavy dependency on proprietary external models (ChatGPT API, Seedream, Hunyuan3D) creates reproducibility concerns; no error analysis for MLLM failures, no fallback mechanisms, error propagation through pipeline not analyzed
Efficiency concerns underexplored: 32 minutes per 9-object scene limits practical deployment; sequential processing despite parallelization potential; scalability to larger scenes unclear

Evaluation methodology has inherent biases: 'best-view' selection favors physically plausible methods (acknowledged by authors in supplementary); test set relatively small (78 samples); LPIPS/DINOv2/CLIP metrics don't directly measure physical plausibility

Limited generalization analysis: tested primarily on standard rectangular tables; only ~2 real-world examples shown; no systematic evaluation of robustness to non-standard geometries, circular/triangular tables, or multi-level surfaces; assumption that vertical axis = 'up' may not generalize

Insufficient ablation studies: individual loss terms (Lsil, Ledge, Lapp) not ablated; loss weights (λs=0.5, λe=0.5, λa=2.0) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis; sequential optimization of rotation vs. translation lacks theoretical justification

MLLM reliability not quantified: camera pose accuracy, commonsense size estimation error, and stacking order determination failures not analyzed; multiple failure points in pipeline but no systematic error analysis or reported failure rates

Design choices lack justification: RMA-Score tolerance τ=0.25 selection unexplained; why commonsense size estimation is robust for scale resolution not clearly argued; what happens when MLLM predictions severely fail (e.g., table size overestimation)

Limited comparison scope: only 4 main baselines; text-to-3D comparison (MesaTask) only qualitative; no comparison with simple baselines or other recent embodied AI scene generation work; no analysis of robustness to different image-to-3D models or MLLM choices

Missing failure case analysis: unclear when RMA-Score selection fails, how performance degrades with scene complexity, robustness to highly occluded inputs; limited discussion of method limitations beyond deferred 'future work'
